connector_reconciliation.evidence_detail: Opposing convexity-defect notches measured on the TOP/BOTTOM axis (notches=3, sides=TB) - not the LEFT/RIGHT axis both real connectors share. Source-visually confirmed (AP-DIAG-018) as a diode symbol (rectangle+triangle), whose apex/rectangle junction produces a top/bottom notch pair ConnectorGeometryDetector's opposing_notches test does not distinguish from a real connector body. detector_topology=inline, detector_confidence=high, bbox=(369,81,28,11).

Opposing convexity-defect notches on the TOP/BOTTOM axis (notches=2, sides=TB). Source-visually confirmed (AP-DIAG-018) as a single wire-color-code character on wire ink, same mechanism as connector-fdd33a2a7f942823. detector_topology=component_attached, detector_confidence=medium, bbox=(365,345,46,10).

Opposing convexity-defect notches on the LEFT/RIGHT axis (notches=3, sides=LR). Source-visually confirmed (AP-DIAG-018): genuine '[MINI]' connector body. detector_topology=inline, detector_confidence=high, bbox=(355,352,17,26).

Opposing convexity-defect notches on the TOP/BOTTOM axis (notches=3, sides=TB) - same axis signature as the other 4 false positives, though the visual read (dense switch-matrix staircase routing) is lower confidence than the other cases (AP-DIAG-018 rated this one LOW). detector_topology=component_attached, detector_confidence=medium, bbox=(420,304,57,51).

Opposing convexity-defect notches on the TOP/BOTTOM axis (notches=2, sides=TB). Source-visually confirmed (AP-DIAG-018) as a single wire-color-code character on wire ink, same mechanism as connector-fdd33a2a7f942823. detector_topology=component_attached, detector_confidence=low, bbox=(371,259,49,10).

Opposing convexity-defect notches measured on the LEFT/RIGHT axis (notches=2, sides=LR) - matches the real TRX300 connector-body profile. Source-visually confirmed (AP-DIAG-018): genuine '[MINI]' connector body. detector_topology=inline, detector_confidence=medium, bbox=(600,289,18,63).

Opposing convexity-defect notches on the TOP/BOTTOM axis (notches=2, sides=TB). Source-visually confirmed (AP-DIAG-018) as the wire-color text label 'G/R' sitting on wire ink; text glyph strokes above/below the wire's own horizontal baseline produce a top/bottom notch pair. No TextRegionDetector region overlaps this box (recognition_input.json) - this label is below that detector's own scale, so a downstream text-region exclusion check would not have caught it either. detector_topology=unknown, detector_confidence=low, bbox=(371,249,49,10).

evidence.methodology: Part A and Part B were established by direct execution of standalone C++ programs reproducing the exact production algorithms (ConnectorGeometryDetector's contour/convexity-defect pipeline; ShapeDetector's detect_circles, including bounded_by_crossing_lines) against the same-run normalized source image (artifacts/recognition/source_normalized.png), not sampling or visual estimation alone. Part C was established by direct reading of src/topology/distribution_decomposer.cpp's net-construction control flow, cross-referenced against the same-run extraction_audit.json's wires/endpoints/nets data. No detector or extraction source file was modified to perform this investigation - only standalone, uncommitted scratch programs that duplicate read-only logic for measurement.
source_visual_corrections: AP-DIAG-018 characterized the 21 DIAGRAM_SYMBOL candidates as 'filled junction dots'. Direct re-inspection at the EXACT bounding boxes (not a wider surrounding crop) shows most are blank grid-gap space; a real dot sometimes sits nearby but outside the candidate's own box. The corrected mechanism is documented in circular_symbol_reconciliation; AP-DIAG-018's functional conclusion (not real components, should not have been promoted) is unchanged.
